who: Adam G. Beaver, historian of early modern Spain and the Mediterranean, Princeton faculty member, PhD Harvard 2008.

evidence.says: Identifies Adam G Beaver's field as Spain and the Renaissance Mediterranean and his doctorate as Harvard University, 2008.
Princeton announced in June 2016 that Adam Beaver, assistant professor of history, was leaving for Harvard effective July 1.
The 2010 Renaissance Quarterly review of Clio and the Crown identifies its author as Adam G Beaver, Princeton University.
The authority heading is Beaver, Adam G.; its source is Steven Ozment's A mighty fortress (2004), crediting Adam G. Beaver.

notes: Exact expanded name, Harvard doctorate and Princeton appointment agree with the supervisor record.

who: Saul Benison, historian of medicine, science and oral history, University of Cincinnati 1969–1990, PhD Columbia 1953.

evidence.says: The AHA obituary records his Columbia history PhD in 1953, Cincinnati history professorship from 1969 until retirement in 1990, and coauthorship of Walter B. Cannon: The Life and Times of a Young Scientist (1987).
The authority heading Benison, Saul is established from Walter B. Cannon (1987).

notes: Degree, institution, period and the authority's identifying work agree.

who: Edward J. Berbusse, historian of Latin America and United States–Latin American relations at Fordham University.

LC identifies Edward Joseph Berbusse, with usage Edward J. Berbusse, and cites his Origins of the Catholic Church (1984).

who: Albert I. Berger, historian at the University of North Dakota, PhD in history from Northern Illinois University.

evidence.says: UND's record for Kenneth Lansdale Smith's Education in the large names Albert I Berger as first advisor; it records a Doctor of Arts dissertation awarded January 23, 2002.
The author biography identifies Albert I. Berger as associate professor of history and peace studies at UND and lists The Magic That Works among his publications.
Cornell's September 1979 alumni publication reports that Albert I Berger recently received a history PhD from Northern Illinois University.
The authority expands Albert I. Berger to Albert Isaac Berger and cites The magic that works (1984).

notes: Direct advisor identification and the shared work establish this candidate. UND gives 2002 and a DA for Smith, versus the supplied AHA year 2001; Berger's exact PhD year was not independently verified.

who: John Andrew Bernstein, historian of European intellectual history at the University of Delaware, PhD Harvard.

Delaware identifies John Bernstein as professor emeritus of history, specializing in European moral philosophy and the idea of progress.

who: Scott Berthelette, historian of New France and Indigenous North America at Queen's University, PhD Saskatchewan 2020.

evidence.says: Queen's lists Berthelette as associate professor of history, PhD University of Saskatchewan 2020, and author of Heirs of an Ambivalent Empire (2022).
The university profile states that he completed his Saskatchewan PhD in January 2020 and describes his dissertation on New France and the Hudson Bay watershed.
The authority heading Berthelette, Scott is established from Heirs of an ambivalent empire (2022).

notes: Exact degree and institution match; the shared book connects the LC identity to the Queen's historian.

who: Richard Bienvenu, historian of France and modern European intellectual history at the University of Missouri, retired 2006.

LC's Richard Bienvenu authority cites The ninth of Thermidor (1968) and The utopian vision of Charles Fourier (1983).

notes: The shared identifying book connects the authority to Missouri; the faculty period includes 1998. The Harvard degree year was not independently verified.
